oneLiner: A merchant builder of superconducting quantum computers selling a handful of systems a year to governments and labs. The market is betting that fidelity keeps scaling toward a ~1,000-qubit machine before the cash pile runs down, and is paying for that roadmap, not for revenue.

verdict.stance: Cautious - a funded option priced as a business
verdict.summary: Q3 2026 showed both halves of the story: the technology milestone was met and the CHIPS award became definitive, while revenue fell to $1.4M, R&D rose 70% and the full-year guide now hangs on one customer acceptance in December. Our base case (FY2027 revenue ~$30M at ~100x EV/Sales) is worth slightly less than the stock, the bear case about a third of it and the bull case roughly double, so the probability-weighted value sits a little below the price with no cash-flow support underneath. The treasury removes solvency risk but not valuation risk. We would move to Neutral if Q4 delivers the ~$9M the guide needs and a second system order is announced for 2027, and stay Cautious or worse if C-DAC acceptance slips or the quarterly cash decline stays above $40M.
wtb: Q4 2026 revenue reaches ~$9M, taking FY2026 to the ~$20M guide; that requires C-DAC to accept the 108-qubit system by Dec 31, 2026.
FY2027 revenue is at least ~$30M from more than one system sale, so that 2026 is a base and not a one-off (first read at the Q4 report, ~Mar 2027).
The 300+ qubit system arrives by mid-2028 at ~99.7% median two-qubit fidelity, with the 99.5% reached on 108 qubits holding as chiplets grow.
Cash and investments stay above ~$350M at end-2027 (Siberforge estimate, including CHIPS draws) without restarting the ATM, and the market still pays ~100x sales for the roadmap.

bear.why: FY2027 revenue ~$18M: C-DAC proves a one-off, no comparable system order follows and revenue falls back to Novera units and development contracts. Fidelity gains stall as chiplets grow, opex keeps rising and quantum sentiment fades, so the market pays ~40x sales - cash plus a modest technology premium.

base.why: FY2027 revenue ~$30M: C-DAC is accepted, one or two further government systems are recognised in 2027 and the first CHIPS tranche funds part of the build-out. The roadmap stays on schedule toward the mid-2028 system but there is still no commercial advantage, so the stock remains a funded option at ~100x sales.

bull.why: FY2027 revenue ~$45M: several national-lab systems ship, the 300+ qubit machine is visibly ahead of schedule with fidelity at or above 99.7%, and later CHIPS tranches are released. Rigetti is treated as the West's merchant superconducting supplier and the market pays ~180x sales, a scarcity multiple.

scenarioModel.note: Value per share = (FY2027 revenue x EV/Sales + net cash) / shares, using the page's current share count and net cash; e.g. base: $30M x 100 = $3.0B of enterprise value, plus net cash, divided by ~334M shares. The page's net-cash figure is above the $497.1M of cash and investments reported at Sep 30, 2026, which flatters every case by roughly $0.90 a share, and burn through 2027 will reduce it further. At this revenue scale the multiple is really the price of the roadmap option, not a statement about sales. The table rounds revenue to $0.0B; the dollar figures are in each case text. Inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Is ~$20M of 2026 revenue a new base, or one system sale?
debates.bull: Nine-month 2026 revenue of $10.9M is already above all of FY2025 ($7.1M), driven by $7.1M of point-in-time equipment sales; governments in India, the UK and the US are buying on-premises systems, and Rigetti is one of very few vendors that will sell one.
debates.bear: Quarterly growth swung from +199% and +185% in the first half to -28% in Q3; revenue fell 18.5% a year over the last three fiscal years, and the guide needs ~$9M in Q4 from a single $8.4M C-DAC order whose acceptance is the customer's call. Government entities were 81.5% of Q3 revenue.
debates.view: Treat 2026 as a lumpy step-up, not a run-rate. We assume C-DAC is accepted but put FY2027 at ~$30M only if a second and third system follow; without a named 2027 order the bear case is the more likely path.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 revenue and any announced system order for 2027 delivery
signpost.threshold: Q4 at or above ~$9M plus a new system order = base holds; Q4 below $5M (acceptance slipped) = bear
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report, ~early Mar 2027 (date not yet announced)

debates.q: Does fidelity keep rising as the qubit count scales?
debates.bull: Cepheus-1-108Q moved from ~99.1% median two-qubit fidelity in August to the 99.5% milestone in Q3, with 99.7% on a 50-qubit sublattice; the chiplet approach and 50-70ns gates are a credible path to error correction at speed.
debates.bear: The sublattice numbers show fidelity still falls as more qubits are included (99.7% on 50, 99.6% on 80, 99.5% on 108); the next step needs 36-qubit chiplets, new cryostats and faster readout at once, and IBM and Google are on the same modality with far larger budgets.
debates.view: This is the debate that sets the multiple, and so far Rigetti has hit its dates. We keep the roadmap on schedule in the base case but give no credit for the ~1,000-qubit target until the 300+ qubit system exists.

signpost.metric: Median two-qubit fidelity on the largest deployed system; first 36-qubit-chiplet results
signpost.threshold: 99.5% or better held on a system larger than 108 qubits by end-2027 = bullish; a slip of the mid-2028 date or fidelity below 99.5% at scale = bearish
signpost.when: Roadmap updates through 2027; 300+ qubit system due mid-2028

debates.q: Does the cash last to the milestone without more dilution?
debates.bull: No debt, no ATM issuance in the first nine months of 2026, and the CHIPS award adds up to $100M ($43.9M available at signing, $29.9M and $26.2M on milestones). At the nine-month pace the treasury covers roughly four years.
debates.bear: Operating losses are more than 5x revenue on a trailing basis and widening: Q3 R&D rose 70% YoY, nine-month capex of $42.6M was 3x the prior year, and cash and investments fell $44.2M in Q3 alone. The CHIPS money cost 7.74M shares, and diluted shares were up 11.7% YoY through Q2.
debates.view: Solvency is not the issue; the price of staying funded is. The dilution rate is falling as the 2025 raises are lapped (Q3 weighted diluted shares +4% YoY), but at ~$45M a quarter the pile is under three years, so we expect management to sell stock again into any rally.

signpost.metric: Quarterly decline in cash and investments; ATM or other equity issuance
signpost.threshold: Decline back under ~$35M a quarter with no new issuance = bull point; above $45M or an ATM restart = bear

thesis: The balance sheet buys the roadmap time. Roughly half a billion dollars of cash and investments against no debt, plus the CHIPS award, funds the build to the mid-2028 system without a forced raise.

The technical milestones are being met on schedule. The 36-qubit multichip system shipped in mid-2025 and the 108-qubit machine hit its fidelity target in Q3 2026, which is the track record the 300+ qubit date rests on.

Washington has made it a funded domestic supplier. The August letter of intent became a definitive agreement in September, with the Commerce Department taking an equity stake - a stronger signal than a grant, and non-debt funding for readout, cryogenics and fabrication.
System sales have arrived, in lumps. Nine-month 2026 revenue more than doubled on equipment sales, and on-premises machines for national programmes are a market IBM and Google do not serve.

Superconducting speed is the physics bet. Gates of 50-70ns are orders of magnitude faster than trapped-ion or neutral-atom operations; if error correction makes every modality usable, throughput decides the winner.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Nov 10). Revenue of $1.4M was down 28% YoY and well below the first half's $9.5M, because no system sale was recognised in the quarter; nine-month revenue of $10.9M is still up 110%. Costs moved the other way: R&D rose 70% to $25.5M and the operating loss widened to $33.2M from $20.5M. The GAAP net loss of $3.1M is flattered by a $25.3M non-cash warrant gain; the non-GAAP loss nearly doubled to $20.5M. Cash and investments ended at $497.1M with no debt, down $44.2M in the quarter as capex stepped up for cryogenic capacity. The disclosure that matters most is the CHIPS agreement signed Sep 4: up to $100M over a period of up to five years in three tranches ($43.9M at signing, $29.9M and $26.2M at the Department's discretion on milestones), in exchange for 7,739,938 shares at an implied $12.92, with repayment rights if project milestones are missed. No cash had been received by quarter-end, per a secondary summary of the 10-Q.
guidanceProse: FY2026 revenue is guided to approximately $20M, explicitly assuming C-DAC accepts its 108-qubit system and the revenue is recognised in Q4; that implies ~$9.1M in Q4 against an order reported at $8.4M in the 10-Q, so acceptance timing decides the year. There is no 2027 revenue guide; the CFO said 2027 capex should be similar to 2026 (per a call summary). The roadmap was updated: a 300+ qubit system at ~99.7% median two-qubit fidelity with gates below 60ns by mid-2028, then ~1,000 qubits at ~99.9% and below 50ns in roughly three years, achieved by packing more qubits into one dilution refrigerator (36-qubit chiplets, new cryostat architecture) instead of networking fridges. Management said it is focused on the organic roadmap, not revenue-driven M&A.

guide.label: FY26 revenue guide
guide.sub: needs ~$9M in Q4 on C-DAC acceptance | 300+ qubits by mid-2028

segments: On-premises systems: 9-qubit Novera QPUs through Cepheus 36Q-108Q full-stack systems for national labs and quantum centres (C-DAC India 108Q, UK NQCC 36Q); the bulk of revenue in quarters when a system is recognised.
Development contracts and government programmes: AFRL and other agency work, now joined by the CHIPS R&D award (accounted for as funding, not revenue).
Cloud QCaaS access via partners; small and not the strategic focus.
competitive: IonQ (trapped ion): Q3 2026 revenue $173.8M (+336% YoY, including $83.5M from the acquired SkyWater foundry) and an FY2026 guide of $505-515M - more than 25x Rigetti's guided year. Rigetti's counter is gate speed, not scale.

IBM: the superconducting incumbent with an in-house fab, a roadmap to large-scale fault tolerance by 2029 and enterprise distribution Rigetti cannot match. Rigetti competes by selling on-premises systems IBM will not.
D-Wave (QBTS): Q2 2026 revenue $3.1M; annealing serves a different problem class but competes for the same speculative capital.
Google Quantum AI: Willow (Dec 2024) validated superconducting error correction but Google does not sell hardware; its results set the technical bar.
IQM (listed Aug 2026): direct competitor in on-premises superconducting systems for research institutions, especially in Europe.
moat: Rigetti's edge is credible full-stack superconducting engineering at merchant scale: chiplet architecture, its own Fab-1 and fidelity within reach of IBM on systems it will actually sell. That is rare, but it is not yet a moat: quantum advantage is undemonstrated, switching costs are nil while workloads are experimental, and IBM and Google outspend it by orders of magnitude on the same modality. Government sponsorship is the nearest thing to a durable advantage today.
risks: The price needs growth the record does not show. The reverse DCF needs revenue to compound about 113% a year for eight years, against a decline of 18.5% a year over the last three fiscal years; nothing in Q3 narrows that gap.

Revenue is single-order risk. One acceptance decides whether FY2026 is ~$20M or ~$11M, and the customer base is almost entirely government; a slipped delivery or a budget delay moves a year, not a quarter.

Losses are widening ahead of revenue. Trailing operating losses exceed 5x revenue and trailing capex is about twice revenue, with R&D and cryogenic spending still stepping up; operating leverage is years away.

Dilution is the funding model. The share count rose at a double-digit rate through mid-2026 on the 2025 raises, the CHIPS award was paid for in stock, and management has shown it will sell shares into strength.

The CHIPS money is conditional. Two of three tranches are released at the Department's sole discretion, the government holds licence and march-in rights over funded IP, and missed project dates allow it to demand repayment as a debt.
catalysts: By Dec 31, 2026: C-DAC customer acceptance of the 108-qubit system (debate 1).
~Early Mar 2027 (date not announced): Q4 and FY2026 results - Q4 revenue vs the ~$9M needed, any 2027 framework, cash decline (debates 1, 3).
2027: second and third CHIPS tranches ($29.9M, $26.2M) on milestones; milestone dates are not disclosed (debate 3).
Through 2027: first 36-qubit-chiplet systems and fidelity updates on the path to 300+ qubits (debate 2).
Mid-2028: 300+ qubit system at ~99.7% median two-qubit fidelity (debate 2).

valPresets.note: FCF is deeply negative and will stay so; revenue mode compounds from the trailing base (FY2026 is guided to ~$20M). A 50% CAGR from $20M reaches ~$500M in eight years - roughly what a durable government and HPC franchise could support; the bull path requires demonstrated quantum advantage and merchant scale. Net cash cushions the downside but is a minor part of the value.
